subject: Provisional uptime anchoring & deferred credit allocation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Liang <tom.liang@airwise.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provisional uptime anchoring & deferred credit allocation

Tom —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m sharing a concise proposal to address Airwise’s concern about tight regional maintenance windows and potential monthly fluctuations in availability during your onboarding ramp.

Proposal (high level):
- Temporary uptime anchor: For month 1–3 post-cutover, Redwood will set a provisional uptime floor of 99.0% for the US region (instead of the standard 99.95%). This is intended to give both teams runway during the initial load-in and regional optimizations.
- Deferred credits: If uptime falls below the standard 99.95% after month 3, Redwood will apply a deferred monthly credit mechanic for months 1–3 tied to a cap (see attached calculator). Credits would be rolled forward and reconciled on month 4 once steady-state metrics are established.
- Fixed monthly allowance: To simplify procurement, we can offer a fixed monthly credit allowance option (rounded bucket) instead of per-incident pro-rata credits — useful for finance planning.

Attached: redwood_sla_draft_v3.pdf (SLA language with bracketed variables) and a simple monthly-credit-calculator.xlsx that demonstrates the deferred-credit math and cap.

As next steps, if this approach sounds reasonable, I’ll route a short note to legal and finance and ask them to review the bracketed terms. I’m happy to walk through the calculator with Priya and your procurement team.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_sla_draft_v3.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: monthly-credit-calculator.xlsx (Excel)

From: Tom Liang <tom.liang@airwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@airwise.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional uptime anchoring & deferred credit allocation

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few clarifying questions from our side before we loop in procurement/legal: 

1) On the provisional uptime floor — is the 99.0% floor only for planned maintenance (regional infra tuning) or all causes (including unplanned incidents) during months 1–3?
2) Deferred credits: can you show an example where the deferred credits hit the cap? We need to model worst-case billing impact for the CFO.
3) Fixed monthly allowance: curious if the allowance reduces our ability to claim incident-level credits in the same month (i.e., is it mutually exclusive?).

If you can send an annotated example and confirm scope (planned vs unplanned), we’ll run it by Priya (procurement) and loop in legal for any unusual carveouts.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Liang | Head of Site Reliability
Airwise Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fw: Provisional uptime anchoring & deferred credit allocation

Laura / Ben —

Looping you both in. Airwise asked three specific clarifications (see below). My recommended approach:

- Scope: Make the provisional 99.0% floor apply to all unplanned incidents and planned maintenance that occurs as part of the onboarding execution plan we ship to them. We can limit the scope by defining "onboarding maintenance" windows in the doc — that keeps us flexible.
- Cap example: See the attached calculator; I prepared a worst-case scenario where month 1 sees 12 hours of downtime — the deferred credit under the cap equals roughly 30% of their monthly committed spend (we can adjust cap to a fixed $ value or percentage).
- Fixed allowance: Offer it as an alternative — if Airwise elects the fixed monthly allowance, it replaces incident-level credits for those first three months only; afterwards we revert to standard per-incident remediation credits. That makes finance predictable.

Requesting quick approvals to offer the fixed-allowance option and to confirm the onboarding scope definition. If approved, I’ll send the annotated SLA (track-changes) and an example invoice reconciliation flow to Priya.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Re: Provisional uptime anchoring & deferred credit allocation

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the breakdown and the calculator walkthrough earlier today. Procurement and legal spoke and we’re broadly supportive of the provisional anchor + deferred credit model with two edits: 

1) We’d like the cap expressed as a dollar amount tied to a monthly committed spend (not only %). Example: cap = lesser of 25% of monthly committed spend or $50,000 for months 1–3. That keeps our executive approvers comfortable.
2) We need the definition of "onboarding maintenance" included explicitly so it cannot be used as a general planned-maintenance carveout beyond month 3. Suggest language: "Onboarding maintenance refers to scheduled activities documented in the onboarding runbook and agreed by both parties prior to the start of the provisioning window."

If Redwood can accept those two edits, we’ll have legal draft a short amendment and route it for countersignature. Otherwise the rest of the SLA looks workable.

Appreciate the responsiveness —
Priya Rao
Procurement Manager | Airwise Analytics
